title: Efficient Open Modification Spectral Library Searching in High-Dimensional Space with Multi-Level-Cell Memory
problem: Open Modification Search (OMS) for mass spectrometry analysis encounters exponentially growing search scope. Existing OMS accelerators have limited parallelism and fail to scale effectively with increasing data volumes.
motivation: OMS enables discovery of modified peptides in mass spectrometry analysis, which is critical for proteomics research.
method: The approach stores more data by using multi-level-cell RRAM (resistive memory where each cell holds multiple values by encoding them at different voltage levels), increasing storage capacity by 3x. Instead of shuttling data between memory and processors—which is slow—it performs calculations directly on the memory. It uses hyperdimensional computing, which represents data in very high-dimensional space and tolerates errors (working correctly even when up to 10% of memory values are wrong), enabling massive hardware parallelism. The design was validated on a fabricated MLC RRAM chip.
key_novelty: Combining multi-level-cell RRAM with error-tolerant hyperdimensional computing to speed up Open Modification Search by performing calculations directly in memory.
contributions: MLC RRAM design achieving 3x storage capacity increase
In-memory computing architecture for OMS achieving 77x speedup
Hyperdimensional computing framework tolerating up to 10% memory errors
2-3 orders of magnitude energy efficiency improvement over existing approaches
